title: August and the Cover
premise: Theo Blackwood has spent a decade erasing problems for the Meridian Group, an embassy that exists only in sealed annexes, until Flight 447 disappears from every database mid-flight while carrying the one witness who could expose her recruitment. Following the vanished plane's ghost trail through Lisbon, Tbilisi, and a decommissioned listening post in the Azores, she discovers the Cover—the training program that made her—has been repurposed to disappear its own graduates. To survive, Theo must burn the network that built her, choosing between the handler who raised her and the defector analyst who taught her to want a life outside the work. In the end she trades her own records for the truth, walking out of the ashes officially nonexistent but finally belonging to herself.
about_author: Juniper Blackwood is the pen name of a former policy analyst who spent years adjacent to the world of quiet diplomacy before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose loyalties are their most dangerous possessions.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A routine scrub: she erases a diplomat's affair from three databases in Vienna, savoring the competence of clean work. Her handler, Voss, radios praise that feels like ownership. Emotional beat: the comfort of invisibility, established just before it shatters.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Monitoring a red-eye from Lisbon, she watches the flight record dissolve mid-air—passenger manifest, transponder logs, even her own access history of it. The witness aboard is Elias Marchetti, the analyst who once refused to recruit her. Beat: dread arriving as a data anomaly.

chapters.title: Ghost Manifest
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, with a brief interlude from air traffic controller Nadia Costa. Theo traces who else touched the file and finds her own signature forged on the deletion. Someone inside is framing her. Beat: paranoia taking root in familiar corridors.

chapters.title: Voss's Lesson
chapters.summary: Theo confronts Voss in the embassy's windowless annex; he deflects with a new assignment and a warning about loyalty being the only currency. Flashback to her recruitment at nineteen. Beat: love and duty entangled in the person who trained her.

chapters.title: Lisbon Rain
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. She goes off-book to Lisbon, finding Nadia Costa alive but terrified; the controller saw the plane land at a closed military strip. First contact from Elias via dead-drop—a message only Theo would understand. Beat: first ally outside the machine.

chapters.title: The Azores File
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Hiding in Ponta Delgada, he decrypts fragments showing the Cover program was never shut down—it was privatized, selling disappearance as a service. He reaches for Theo because she's the only graduate he trusts. Beat: hope as a calculated risk.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Protocol
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo and Elias meet in a fish market, all tradecraft and suspicion softening into recognition. He shows her the ledger: forty-seven graduates erased, herself listed next. Beat: belonging offered by someone who knew her before the training.

chapters.title: Forty-Seven Names
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. She cross-references the erased graduates and finds they were eliminated after requesting release. The pattern points to Deputy Director Hale, Voss's superior. Beat: grief for colleagues she never knew she mourned.

chapters.title: Tbilisi Cold
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Following money through a Georgian shell bank, she's ambushed by a cleanup team—graduates like her, sent to erase her. She wins ugly, wounded, and realizes the network will spend its own children. Beat: the cost of the skills she was given.

chapters.title: What Voss Built
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Ordered to bring Theo in or bury her, he reviews her file and remembers the girl he recruited, torn between the institution that made him and the protégée who was his one honest act. Beat: a handler's love expressed as control.

chapters.title: The Listening Post
chapters.summary: Theo and Elias infiltrate the decommissioned Azores station where Flight 447 actually landed. They find the hangar converted into a processing center—and evidence the plane's passengers are alive, held as leverage. Beat: horror reframing the mission as rescue.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Captured briefly by Hale's people, she's offered partnership: help sell the Cover's services globally, keep Elias as collateral. She sees her whole future laid out in gilded chains. Beat: temptation of power versus integrity.

chapters.title: Escape Velocity
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Using escape techniques Voss taught her, she breaks out, acutely aware she's weaponizing her inheritance against itself. Elias extracts her by sea; between them, something unspoken finally gets said. Beat: love chosen over duty, tentatively.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Officially declared rogue, her accounts frozen, face distributed to every allied service. She and Elias plan to torch the network using its own archive. Beat: freedom and destitution arriving together.

chapters.title: The Archive Key
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The full Cover archive sits behind a key held by Voss personally. Elias argues trust is a trap; Theo insists Voss can be turned. Their first real fight. Beat: two survival philosophies colliding.

chapters.title: Vienna Reckoning
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. She confronts Voss alone in the old annex, laying out Hale's crimes. Voss reveals he kept the key as insurance for years—he was always waiting for someone worth giving it to. Beat: the mentor's confession, love finally unclenched into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Betrayal Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Handing over the key triggers a silent alarm; Hale's team closes in. Voss stays behind to hold the door, telling Theo the only thing he ever gave her freely was the exit. Beat: devastating cost of the turn.

chapters.title: Ash Network
chapters.summary: Theo and Elias's POV, alternating. From a safehouse they detonate the archive—forty-seven names, client lists, the Cover's entire architecture—released simultaneously to twelve newsrooms. Beat: catharsis, immediately shadowed by retaliation incoming.

chapters.title: The Hangar Standoff
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Hale moves to destroy the Azores site and its hostages. Theo leads a ragged team of surviving graduates against the facility. Beat: the erased reclaiming the place that erased them.

chapters.title: Flight 447 Lands
chapters.summary: Climax. Theo's POV. In the hangar, she faces Hale among the freed passengers as the world's press arrives to see the impossible plane come home. Hale falls—not to a bullet but to exposure, arrested on camera. Beat: victory witnessed, undeniable.

chapters.title: Afterimage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Testifying under protection, she watches her own records entered into evidence—the self she was, archived and closed. Voss's funeral is attended by no one official, so she attends for everyone. Beat: mourning the father the system let him barely be.

chapters.title: August
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Theo's POV. Months later, officially nonexistent but legally free, Theo and Elias share a rented house where August light comes through ordinary windows. She takes small cases helping people disappear by choice, not force. Beat: belonging, finally, on her own terms.
